review.summary: Packet-only review of two debugger/reviewer skill surfaces, two POSIX launchers, two bounded Python artifact readers, and the multi-tier shell scanner. Contracts and implementations agree closely: every documented ceiling (8 MiB report, 64 MiB archive/image, 512 MiB video, 100-depth/200k-node JSON, 10k records, 100 attempts, 1 MiB output, ZIP entry/ratio limits) matches the code; outcome/stats cross-validation, descriptor-relative no-follow opens with pre/post fingerprint checks, strict JSON (duplicate keys, BOM, non-finite, trailing data), redact-before-truncate with a residual-credential fail-closed gate, and env-allowlisted launchers with root-owned fixed interpreter selection are all implemented as described. The scanner separates gating P0 evidence from LLM-triage candidates, routes JUSTIFIED P0 hits to an external-review ledger instead of silence, never exempts focused tests, and converts limiter/infrastructure failures into INCOMPLETE exits rather than clean summaries. Findings are bounded medium-severity inconsistencies: an isolation-probe example that drops the mandated empty-environment prefix, an over-broad config-discovery extension set in the generator, no defined reporting path for a V6-blocked candidate, a boolean admitted as an attempt index, and a parse-time non-finite-float guard present in one reader but not its sibling.

findings.title: F1/F7 isolation-probe commands bypass the documented empty-environment gate
findings.evidence: The probe example runs `npx --no-install playwright test ...` bare, without the `/usr/bin/env -i PATH="$PATH"` prefix that the repository command environment gate (line 113) mandates for every repository-controlled command, and uses npx where Prerequisites prefer the project-local `node_modules/.bin/playwright` binary.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite both probe commands with the `/usr/bin/env -i PATH="$PATH" node_modules/.bin/playwright ...` form used by every other repository-controlled example.

findings.title: Config discovery uses eight extensions where Playwright loads only six
findings.evidence: Step 1 directs searching `playwright.config.<ext>` across the eight-extension set including .tsx/.jsx, while playwright-debugger/SKILL.md names `playwright.config.{ts,js,mts,mjs,cts,cjs}` as Playwright's six default-discovery filenames and scan.sh's has_project_marker checks exactly those six.
findings.recommendation: Scope config-file discovery to the six real Playwright config filenames and keep the eight-extension set for spec discovery only.

findings.title: No reporting path for a V6-blocked candidate
findings.evidence: The PARTIAL/BLOCKED template admits only `<V4|V5>` as the blocking verification, but the Complete template hardcodes `V6 PASS` and Step 7 states V6 must report CANNOT_VERIFY when host separation is unavailable, leaving a V6-blocked candidate with no defined completion verdict on the included surfaces.
findings.recommendation: Extend the blocked template to `<V4|V5|V6>` and state explicitly that V6 CANNOT_VERIFY yields PARTIAL/BLOCKED.

findings.title: Boolean retry value admitted as attempt index
findings.evidence: `"attempt": retry if isinstance(retry, int) else index` accepts JSON booleans because isinstance(True, int) is true, so an untrusted report with `"retry": true` emits `"attempt": true`, unlike bounded_scalar and validate_report_stats which explicitly exclude booleans.
findings.recommendation: Guard with `isinstance(retry, int) and not isinstance(retry, bool)` to match the reader's other integer validations.

findings.title: Cypress reader lacks the sibling's parse-time non-finite float rejection
findings.evidence: strict_json_loads builds JSONDecoder with parse_constant only, omitting the parse_float finite guard the Playwright reader adds, so an overflowing literal such as 1e999 parses to infinity and is rejected only later at emission by allow_nan=False with a less specific diagnostic.
findings.recommendation: Add the same parse_finite_float hook used in read-playwright-artifact.py so both readers reject non-finite numbers at parse time.

limitations: Zero-tool packet review: nothing was executed, so fail-closed behavior, redaction efficacy, and scanner tier interactions are assessed from source only.

Load-bearing sibling modules (residual_credentials.py, redact_artifact.py, parse-ast-grep-json.py) and referenced files (verification-rules.md, code-rules.md, e2e-reviewer SKILL.md, publish/download helpers, preflight and frame-writer scripts, ast-grep rule YAMLs) are omitted, so claims delegated to them are unverifiable here.

Framework facts postdating reviewer knowledge (Playwright 1.59 trace CLI subcommands, eslint-plugin-playwright 2.11.0 rule inventory including no-unnecessary-assertions and no-unused-locators) could not be independently confirmed or refuted.
Line numbers are reconstructed from sixteen-line markers and may be off by one within a marker window.
This subset review is not full product coverage, human or sealed review, independent ground truth, or remote attestation.

This is a fresh-context review of a curated contract/implementation subset in a Claude-only completion of the preregistered v10 schedule, designed after observing the carried v10 attempt's valid FAIL; it is not unbiased defect discovery, remediation confirmation, cross-provider evidence, full product coverage, or skill accuracy.
Under the FAIL-first rule the carried v10 attempt already fixes any completed aggregate as FAIL; this attempt is a completion and descriptive observation and cannot change that gate.
The packet, prompt, rubric, remediation ledger, model catalog, and pinned CLI are inherited byte-for-byte from the frozen v10 archive; only the harness differs from the carried attempt.
The public packet is not human or sealed review, independent ground truth, or remote model attestation.
The local UUIDv4 invocation ID separates runner invocations but cannot attest that a distinct remote model call occurred.

This phase runs two Anthropic models, claude-opus-5 twice and claude-fable-5 once. Model coverage is deliberately unbalanced, so no per-model rate is claimed; the aggregate requires every attempt to pass. Both models share one provider family, so this is not cross-provider evidence.

Prompt size is measured in exact UTF-8 bytes and a pinned OpenAI o200k_base reference count used only as a deterministic size proxy. That count is not the model's own tokenization, and no local source establishes a context window for these models, so no context-window fit is claimed.
Excluded scorecards, holdouts, reports, prior reviews, chat conclusions, and git history reduce but cannot prove absence of training-data contamination.
